repair_loop.description: The build-repair cycle lives in _stage_validation() (runner.py lines 805-1134). After initial dotnet build+run via run_dotnet_validation(), the loop enters two sequential repair phases: (1) BUILD REPAIR: up to 2 LLM-driven attempts (max_build_repairs=2 when LLM available and not template_mode). Each attempt extracts compiler stdout/stderr, constructs a repair prompt with the failing code and re-injected REQUIRED/FORBIDDEN constraints (both PDF-specific and per-type), sends it to the LLM, runs semantic validation on the proposed fix (_validate_code + _validate_code_from_constraints), and only writes the fix to disk if it passes semantic checks. Then re-runs dotnet build+run. (2) RUNTIME REPAIR: up to 1 LLM-driven attempt (max_runtime_repairs=1). Classifies the runtime failure via classify_runtime_failure() and only attempts repair if the classification is in the repairable_classifications set (8 known failure types). The repair prompt includes the runtime classification, stdout/stderr, and re-injected constraints. Both loops write evidence to repair-attempts.json and update lifecycle records (mark_build_repaired / mark_run_repaired).
repair_loop.constraint_re_injection: REQUIRED and FORBIDDEN constraints from the generation packet are stored on each project dict at generation time (runner.py line 759-768) and re-injected into repair prompts to prevent semantic regression during repair.
repair_loop.semantic_guard: Before writing any repaired code to disk, _validate_code() and _validate_code_from_constraints() run semantic checks. If the repaired code introduces forbidden patterns or drops required patterns, the repair is rejected and the attempt is logged as failed (lines 883-896 for build, 1004-1016 for runtime).

core_registry_files.purpose: Bootstrap metadata including version and supported families
Catalog of known failure patterns (FP-001 etc.) with affected families/types, enabling is_known_failure() lookups and get_failures_for_type() queries to avoid re-discovering known issues
Catalog of repair strategies (RP-001 etc.) linked to failure IDs via resolves_failure, providing get_repair_for_failure() lookups
Per-family and per-type REQUIRED/FORBIDDEN constraints for LLM prompt steering, served via get_steering_constraints(family, type_name)
Validator rules (VR-001 etc.) with applies_to scoping and IMPLEMENTED/NOT_IMPLEMENTED status, served via get_validator_rules(family, type_name)

healing_registries.integration_status: The HealingIntelligenceLoader is fully implemented with lazy loading, graceful degradation, and query APIs. However, it is NOT directly imported or called from runner.py or code_generator.py. The constraint re-injection in the repair loop uses per_type_constraints from family config (not from the healing loader). The healing registries serve as a persistent knowledge layer for cross-session intelligence but are not wired into the live repair loop at runtime.

gate_evaluation.description: The gate evaluator (evaluate_gates) produces a GateVerdict by checking stage results against a set of gates. Hard-stop stages (load_config, nuget_fetch, dependency_resolution, extraction, reflection, plugin_detection) halt the pipeline on failure. Subsequent gates assess scenario planning, generation, build validation, runtime validation, and reviewer outcomes. Gates produce pass/fail/degraded/blocked/skipped statuses. The gate engine does NOT trigger repair directly -- repair is handled inline within _stage_validation(). Gates evaluate AFTER repair has already been attempted, so gate_build and gate_run reflect post-repair outcomes. A failed gate_build blocks downstream gate_run. The reviewer gate (gate_reviewer) marks examples as backlogged with recommended_fix='Address reviewer feedback and regenerate' but does NOT trigger an automatic re-generation loop.
gate_evaluation.repair_trigger_mechanism: Repair is NOT gate-triggered. It runs unconditionally within _stage_validation() whenever build/run failures are detected and LLM is available (max_build_repairs > 0). Gates only evaluate the final post-repair state.

operational_status_rationale: The build-repair loop in _stage_validation() is fully implemented and operational: it performs up to 2 build repairs and 1 runtime repair per example, with semantic validation guards, constraint re-injection, evidence logging (repair-attempts.json), and lifecycle tracking. The HealingIntelligenceLoader is fully implemented with 22 passing tests and 5 core registries on disk, but serves as a knowledge-layer sidecar rather than being directly wired into the live repair loop. The repair loop uses per_type_constraints from family config instead. The gate evaluator evaluates post-repair results but does not trigger repair itself. Overall: the repair loop is FUNCTIONAL; the healing intelligence layer is FUNCTIONAL but operates as a reference/query system rather than driving the repair loop directly.

constraint_persistence.description: pdf_constraints, family_name, type_short, type_constraints stored on project dict for later re-injection during repair

code_generator_repair.description: generate_example() has its own validation+repair pass (lines 106-150+) for LLM-generated code before it reaches _stage_validation, using _validate_code and constraint checks with max_repairs parameter

reviewer_stage.description: Reviewer runs post-validation, marks failed examples as backlogged with recommended_fix but does NOT trigger automatic re-repair
